text: yeah so this is an interesting problem because we do not want overhang and we do not want it to feel like one side is larger than the other. when i think about it, i think to the sims or fortnite, where a wall is on one grid axis, and it never over or underhangs. regardless of if there is a floor on both sides of it or not. how is that achieved. because the instinct is 'walls sit on the ground, and always on the grid' but that means that floors can never connect because there could be potentially a wall to be placed. one of them has to sacrifice and the wall offset i think is the one that is more problematic
